mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows when FEDFUNDS > 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and housing starts indicate strong economic demand, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows when both GDPC1 and HOUST are rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth in a late-cycle expansion may indicate supply constraints, leading to increased production costs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows during late-cycle expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, which may lead to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 5-day windows following rising RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows when PAYEMS increases by > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates combined with slowing GDP growth indicate stagflation, leading to decreased investor confidence and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows when FEDFUNDS are high and GDPC1 is slowing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4% during a monetary tightening cycle may lead to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows when FEDFUNDS > 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.
